record.paper_title: Some open problems in random matrix theory and the theory of integrable systems
record.original_question: Develop perturbation theory for infinite-dimensional integrable systems in settings where solitons are present and the perturbation no longer becomes asymptotically negligible. A central instance is the focusing cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation with an added perturbation term ε V(|u|)u, especially for solutions lying near k-soliton states with k≥2, together with a detailed description of the long-time asymptotics; related questions include the persistence of Toda shocks and rarefactions under perturbations and perturbations of the sine-Gordon equation relevant to the Fermi-Pasta-Ulam problem.

evidence.quote: It is of great interest to consider perturbations of type (7) for the focusing (cubic) NLS equation, i.e. where the term -2|u|2u is replaced by +2|u|2u.

The solution of (7) in the focusing case in the neighborhood of a k-soliton for (cubic) NLS (k ≥ 2), together with a detailed description of the long-time asymptotics, would be regarded as a very significant development in the theory of PDEs/Mathematical Physics.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the focusing cubic nonlinear Schrödinger (NLS) equation perturbed by a small nonlinear lower-order term:

   i u_t + u_{xx} + 2|u|^2 u + ε V(|u|) u = 0,    (x,t) ∈ ℝ × ℝ,

where ε > 0 is a small parameter and V: [0,∞) → ℝ is a smooth real-valued function (so that the perturbation εV(|u|)u preserves the L^2 norm but is, in general, non-integrable and does not decay or become asymptotically negligible compared to the integrable nonlinearity). The unperturbed equation (ε = 0) is completely integrable by the inverse scattering transform and admits k-soliton solutions for every k ≥ 1.

Develop a perturbation theory for this equation in the regime where solitons are present and the perturbation is not asymptotically negligible. Specifically, accomplish the following:

(a) For initial data u(x,0) lying in a sufficiently small neighborhood (in a suitable function space, e.g. a weighted Sobolev space) of a k-soliton solution of the unperturbed focusing cubic NLS with k ≥ 2, prove global existence and produce a detailed description of the long-time asymptotic behavior of u(x,t) as t → ±∞: identify the emerging soliton parameters (positions, velocities, phases, amplitudes), the dispersive radiation contribution, and any corrections due to the perturbation εV(|u|)u, with explicit error estimates uniform in ε small.

(b) Establish an analogous perturbation theory for the Toda lattice in the presence of shocks and rarefaction waves, showing that such structures persist under small non-integrable perturbations of the lattice equations.

(c) Establish an analogous perturbation theory for the sine-Gordon equation under perturbations of the form relevant to the Fermi–Pasta–Ulam problem, again describing long-time asymptotics in the presence of multi-kink (soliton) configurations.

The goal is a unified asymptotic theory extending the Deift–Zhou nonlinear steepest descent / perturbed Riemann–Hilbert methodology to settings with multi-soliton backgrounds and non-decaying perturbations.
artifact.status_search_result: Significant progress has been made: Deift–Zhou-style perturbative long-time asymptotic results have been extended to perturbations of mKdV and to focusing NLS with nonzero boundary conditions and discrete spectrum, and soliton-resolution results have been obtained. However, a full perturbation theory for the focusing cubic NLS near k-soliton states (k ≥ 2) with general non-decaying perturbation εV(|u|)u, plus the Toda shock/rarefaction and sine-Gordon FPU components, is not fully established and remains an active area of research.

status_evidence.title: Long-Time Asymptotics of A Perturbed Modified KdV Equation
status_evidence.snippet: Extends the perturbative theory of infinite-dimensional integrable systems developed by Deift and Zhou to mKdV; first extension to AKNS hierarchy beyond NLS on the real line.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress on perturbation theory for integrable PDEs has been achieved for related equations.

status_evidence.title: Long-time Asymptotics for the Focusing NLS with Nonzero Boundary Conditions in the Presence of a Discrete Spectrum
status_evidence.snippet: Rigorous characterization of nonlinear interactions between solitons and coherent oscillating structures from localized perturbations in a modulationally unstable medium.
status_evidence.claim: Long-time asymptotics in focusing NLS with solitons and perturbations have been partially analyzed.

status_evidence.title: Long-Time Asymptotics for the Focusing NLS Equation
status_evidence.snippet: Soliton resolution results for focusing NLS using Riemann-Hilbert techniques.
status_evidence.claim: Soliton resolution for focusing NLS is established in the integrable case.
